beats.goal: The learner knows a page is one html element with a head and a body.
beats.content: Every HTML page is one html element with two children. The head holds information about the page, such as its title. The body holds what the reader sees.
beats.question: Before we go on: the title shows on the browser tab. Do you think the title element goes in the head or in the body? Why?

beats.goal: The learner can place common elements.
beats.content: Visible content, such as headings, paragraphs and links, goes in the body. The title and the meta elements go in the head.
beats.question: Predict: if you put an h1 in the head, what will the browser do?

checkpoint.question: In your own words: what is the difference between the head and the body of an HTML page, and where would you put a page title and a heading?
checkpoint.rubric: A good answer says the head holds information about the page (the title goes there) and the body holds the visible content (the heading goes there). Exact wording does not matter.

branches.when: The answer puts the title in the head and the heading in the body.
branches.message: You can tell the head from the body. Next, a link with one planted bug.

branches.when: The answer swaps the two or does not say where either one goes.
branches.message: Let's go over what the head and the body hold once more.
